protocol: 16 independent base images x3trials x3variants; rotate oldauto/newauto/newadaptive order each trial; freshCLI percall; one shared isolatedHOME; model pinned; OS page caches not flushed

boundaries.includes: Fresh CLI process, guard/operation dispatch, image I/O/decode, Tesseract, merge and JSON response
boundaries.builds: Two optimized release binaries; exact SHA256s pinned before/after measurement
boundaries.order: Each variant occupies first/second/third position once per image across3trials

settings.selector: Each base image's identical primary_target or negative_target as text_contains

boundaries.host_load: Uncontrolled concurrent host activity; see post-run load_average_after

conclusion.default_auto: In this paired run newauto median is4.09%aboveoldauto; median matchedpair ratio is2.01%aboveold,29/48pairs slower, with mixed per-case directions. The earlier unpaired~12%default-auto difference did not reproduce at that magnitude. A modest cost or host/run noise remains possible;3trials do not establish causality or a universal regression.
conclusion.adaptive_net: Newadaptive median is14.30%belowOLDauto and17.67%belowNEWauto in this paired corpus run. This is local CLI image-reading time, not device or agent-loop speed.
conclusion.quality: All144calls preserve the same labelled-target/word quality per corresponding image/trial acrossvariants; labelled corpus equality does not prove equal coverage on other screens.
conclusion.claim_guard: Use the paired baseline for net comparisons; do not present same-build~11.9%adaptive-vs-auto from an earlier run as a universal speedup over the oldproduct. Keep the sampled2–4%default-auto timing difference visible rather than claiming no overhead.
